summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of severe Crohn’s disease, status post subtotal colectomy and ileorectal anastomosis, was admitted for a flare characterized by increased watery bowel movements and left lower quadrant abdominal pain. He had recently tapered his prednisone to 20 mg but increased it to 40 mg as symptoms worsened. Stool studies were negative for infectious causes. Imaging revealed active Crohn’s disease in the distal ileum with a new skip lesion, but no abscess or obstruction. MRIs of the spine and hips ruled out epidural abscess and avascular necrosis. He was treated with IV fluids and IV steroids, with gradual improvement in symptoms. He transitioned to oral prednisone, advanced to a regular diet, and was discharged with a plan for steroid tapering, B-complex supplementation, continued B12 injections, and smoking cessation support.
